criteria_quotes: Primary total hip arthroplasty or conversion of a previous intra-articular or implant hip surgery to a hip arthroplasty is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following indications: ... Joint damage or destruction due to osteoarthritis, inflammatory disease, or other chronic condition when ALL of the following requirements have been met:

Physical exam consistent with symptomatic hip arthritis (e.g., pain with passive motion of the hip, antalgic gait, limited motion) unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4, diffuse modified Outerbridge grade 4, or Tonnis grade 3

Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-surgical conservative management (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4) [in the 2025-11-15 version; the 2024-11-17 version stated 'Failure of at least 3 months of non-surgical conservative management (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4, Outerbridge grade 4, or Tonnis grade 3)']
Functional limitation secondary to hip pathology which interferes with the ability to perform age-appropriate daily activities

Imaging evidence of significant joint destruction and cartilage loss, defined as Tönnis grade 3, modified Outerbridge grade III–IV, or Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3–4 [this bullet and the 'limited range of motion, antalgic gait and disabling pain of at least 3 months' duration' bullet appear in the 2021–2024 versions of this same guideline and were consolidated into the 'physical exam' bullet quoted above in the 2025-11-15 revision]
answer.appeal_deadline: 180 days from the date of the notice (2026-08-13), i.e., must be received by 2027-02-09, as stated in the denial letter.
answer.submission_route: The denial letter itself does not print a mailing address, fax number, or portal link for filing the appeal — it only states the 180-day deadline. I could not verify a Missouri-specific commercial appeal mailing address or fax number from public sources, so this detail should be confirmed directly from the member's ID card, Evidence of Coverage/Certificate, or by calling Anthem Member Services before mailing anything.

This can be requested by phone (member services number on the ID card) or in writing referencing the denial notice. The provider's UM/prior-authorization portal (Carelon Medical Benefits Management, which administers Anthem's Musculoskeletal/Joint Surgery program) can also supply the full guideline PDF.
